entityRegistry.name: Firm
entityRegistry.description: Top-level tenant. INVRT is the only Firm in the MVP, but every row in every table carries firm_id so a second Firm can never be reached by a query that forgets to scope.

entityRegistry.name: User
entityRegistry.description: A named person at the Firm. Carries no mandate access on its own; all access is granted through Membership.

entityRegistry.name: Membership
entityRegistry.description: Join between User and Mandate carrying role analyst, lead, partner, or admin. Revoking sets state revoked, which immediately removes retrieve and generate rights (FEAT-001).

entityRegistry.name: Mandate
entityRegistry.description: The engagement workspace and the isolation boundary for retrieval. Carries a restricted flag that excludes it from any firm-wide surface. Every Document, Chunk, Run, Table and Memo hangs off exactly one Mandate.

entityRegistry.name: Document
entityRegistry.description: An uploaded source file. MVP accepts PDF and DOCX only; XLSX and PPTX from FEAT-002 are deferred out of the signed briefing-pack scope.

entityRegistry.name: DocumentChunk
entityRegistry.description: The citation index. A span of text with a resolvable locator (PDF page number, DOCX section heading and paragraph ordinal) plus a denormalised firm_id and mandate_id so an unscoped retrieval query cannot cross mandates.

entityRegistry.name: IngestReport
entityRegistry.description: Per-upload-batch record naming which files indexed and which failed to parse with the parser error, so one corrupt file never blocks the batch (FEAT-002).

entityRegistry.name: ResearchRun
entityRegistry.description: One question executed against one Mandate corpus. no_evidence is a first-class success state, not a failure: it is how the system says the fact is not in the documents rather than inventing a number.

entityRegistry.name: Citation
entityRegistry.description: Link from a claim on a ResearchRun to the DocumentChunk that supports it. A rejected Citation is retained for audit but is filtered out of memo generation unless replaced (FEAT-003).

entityRegistry.name: EvidenceTable
entityRegistry.description: Rows are topics, columns are briefing questions. partial means the fill completed but at least one cell is unverified or not_in_corpus.

entityRegistry.name: EvidenceCell
entityRegistry.description: One row-column intersection. Holds short answer text plus Citations, and records whether the current text came from retrieval or from a human edit. Reruns are per-cell so a 20x8 table shows per-cell progress.

entityRegistry.name: BriefingMemo
entityRegistry.description: The Word work product. The approved state is the human-in-the-loop gate: no DOCX byte stream is served to a browser while the memo is in generated or pending_approval (FEAT-005).

entityRegistry.name: AuditEvent
entityRegistry.description: Append-only. No update or delete path exists in the API. Each AI event stores model provider and version, retrieval chunk ids, actor, mandate id, and answer mode.

entityRegistry.name: RetrievalAgent
entityRegistry.description: Ranks DocumentChunks for a question. Its query is constructed so that firm_id and mandate_id are bound parameters, not model-supplied arguments, which is why a prompt injection in an uploaded document cannot widen its scope.

entityRegistry.name: AnsweringAgent
entityRegistry.description: Turns retrieved chunks into a cited claim. refused is the state it enters when the retrieved context does not support an answer. It has no network tool and no filesystem tool; its only input is the chunk text passed to it.

entityRegistry.name: LlmProvider
entityRegistry.description: Optional external model endpoint. When disabled or unavailable the system runs in extractive mode, quoting source sentences verbatim rather than generating prose, which keeps the no-invented-numbers guarantee true with no vendor dependency.

openDecisions: MVP scope is narrower than the spec-contract MVP phase. The owner signed off the cited briefing pack only, which is FEAT-001 through FEAT-005. FEAT-006 diligence question list is out. FEAT-007 is included only as the append-only AuditEvent entity; the admin audit-pack export surface is out. FEAT-008 is included only as the AI-assisted disclosure and the no-network-tool constraint on AnsweringAgent; vendor no-train contract assertions are out. spec-contract.json still carries signedOff false and needs an explicit decision on whether to sign the full eight-feature MVP or restate it as the five-feature briefing pack.

FEAT-002 names PDF, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX. MVP ingests PDF and DOCX only, because a spreadsheet locator is a cell range rather than a page and needs its own citation model. XLSX and PPTX ingest is deferred.

Retrieval in MVP is PostgreSQL full-text ranking, not vector search. This keeps the install to a stock PostgreSQL with no pgvector extension. The DocumentChunk entity is deliberately storage-agnostic so an embedding column can be added without a state machine change, but recall on paraphrased questions will be materially worse than a vector index until then.

Authentication in MVP is a local user picker against seeded Firm users, not SSO. Membership and role enforcement are real and are the tested boundary; identity proofing is not. This must not be deployed beyond a single trusted machine until an identity provider is wired in.

LlmProvider is optional. With no API key the AnsweringAgent runs extractive-only and quotes source sentences verbatim. This guarantees no invented numbers but produces blunter prose than a generative answer. Whether extractive output is acceptable as a partner-facing first draft is the main thing to learn from the MVP.

Citation acceptance is not required before memo generation in MVP; proposed citations flow through and only rejected ones are filtered. Requiring explicit per-citation acceptance would be a stricter gate and is the obvious next tightening if partners do not trust the pack.
